content: When creating a new disease page, you should begin by typing `__NOTOC__` at the very top of the edit box. This command, enclosed by two underscores on each side, stands for no table of contents and ensures that a table of contents does not appear on the page. Next, you should include the microchapter template you have created for the disease. For example, if the disease is jaundice, you would type `{{Jaundice}}` into the edit box. You must also create a link to the patient information page on the main disease page. For instance, if the disease is pericarditis, you would type the following into the edit box: `'''For patient information, click [link]'''`. This would appear on the page as: For patient information, click here. The square brackets are used to create a hyperlink to the disease page. The text on the left side of the vertical bar within the square brackets specifies the page you are linking to, while the text on the right side specifies the word or phrase that will appear on the page. The statement should be bolded and placed at the top of the edit box, before the `{{CMG}}` template. After this, you should type the template for the Editor-in-Chief, Dr. C. Michael Gibson, by entering `{{CMG}}` into the edit box. The brackets around CMG are curly brackets. On the page, this will appear as: Editor-In-Chief: C. Michael Gibson. Following this, you should type `{{AE}}` into the edit box, which will appear on the page as: Associate Editor(s)-in-Chief:. You would then include your own user template. For example, if your initials are JD (John Doe), you would type `{{JD}}` to link to your user page. This allows readers to learn more about you. Your user page should have been created when you first logged into WikiDoc. If you need instructions on creating a user page, you can find them by clicking the appropriate link. To create your name template, type Template: your initials into the search box. For example, if your name is John Doe, you would search for Template: JD. In the edit box, you would type `[user page link | display name]`. The text on the left side of the vertical line in the square brackets links to your user page, while the text on the right side specifies how your name will appear at the top of the page. After entering this, click save. For example, if John Doe wants his name to appear at the top of the page with a link to his user page, he would type `{{JD}}`. If John Doe were creating a page on jaundice, the edit box would look like this: ``` __NOTOC__ {{Jaundice}} {{CMG}} {{AE}} {{JD}} ``` On the page, this would appear at the top as: Editor-In-Chief: C. Michael Gibson Associate Editor(s)-in-Chief: John Doe After this, you should add a line for synonyms and keywords related to the disease, if applicable. This process is detailed in the next section of the main help page.
